messages:
emily park: hi team, new hire 👋 tried to open a PR to trigger our Buildkite onboarding pipeline but the webhook didn't start. i pushed a branch and opened a PR in the repo, the repo shows the check suite as pending forever. any quick things to check?

omar diaz: welcome emily! first things: did you accept the GitHub App invite for Redwood CI and make sure SSO provision is approved if your org requires it? also check if the repo still has the app installed (org -> installed GitHub Apps).

emily park: i accepted the app invite earlier. PR link: https://github.com/redwood/my-service/pull/12

maria lin: can you paste the PR check logs? if Buildkite didn't receive the webhook we should see no build created in Buildkite. sometimes webhook delivery is failing or the repo was migrated.

emily park: Buildkite shows nothing. github webhook delivery history shows a 404 for POST to our buildkite webhook URL endpoint.

devops-bot: Reminder: Buildkite's GitHub App used for webhooks relies on the app installation and a valid webhook endpoint secret. If the app was re-installed or the webhook target changed during a migration, delivery can 404.

paul chen: i saw a recent migration where we swapped proxies for the webhook endpoint and forgot to update the GitHub App's webhook target URL for some repos. emily, can you confirm the repo is under the org where the app is installed (not a personal fork)?

emily park: this PR is against the org repo. i forked locally then pushed the branch to the org remote.

omar diaz: two investigative steps: 1) GitHub -> repo -> Settings -> Webhooks -> check delivery history for the Buildkite app webhook; 2) Buildkite -> Project -> Settings -> check the repository URL and webhook secret. i can't access the org webhooks without ops perms, pinging infra.

maria lin: also check whether the repo name contains a dot or uppercase letter — our proxy route uses strict regex and that caused 404s once. unlikely but worth verifying.

(omar checks infra)
omar diaz: infra confirmed we recently rotated the webhook proxy and updated most app installations, but `my-service` got missed because it was archived briefly. infra will re-install the app on that repo and re-sync webhooks.

emily park: thanks! any quick workaround to run the onboarding CI while infra fixes the webhook?

paul chen: you can manually trigger the Buildkite pipeline from the UI if you have access (Buildkite -> Pipelines -> onboarding -> Trigger build), or run the local steps in the README. i can trigger a build on your branch if you drop the branch name here.

emily park: branch is feature/emily/onboard-ci. please trigger if that's ok.

paul chen: triggered a manual build and attached logs: https://buildkite.com/redwood/onboarding/builds/78 — it started but failed at checkout with 403 when fetching the repo.

emily park: 403 on checkout? i can clone the org repo locally with my token.

maria lin: Buildkite uses the GitHub App installation token for checkout. if the app isn't properly installed on that repo or the app token lacks repo scope due to SSO restrictions, checkout will 403.

omar diaz: infra reinstalled the app and re-synced webhooks. try opening a small dummy PR to retrigger a webhook event.

emily park: opened another tiny PR. webhook delivery now shows 200. new Buildkite build started and is running.

(2 minutes later)
emily park: build passed! thanks everyone for the quick help. learned: accept GitHub App + ensure app installed on repo + infra webhook proxy must match.

maria lin: adding a note to the onboarding checklist: when a PR doesn't trigger CI -> check GH App install on repo, webhook delivery history (404/403), SSO approval, and ability to trigger manual Buildkite builds.

paul chen: tagging this thread into the onboarding doc for visibility. emily, welcome again and ping me if you want walkthrough of manual trigger steps. :wave:
